title: Causal Attention for Interpretable and Generalizable Graph Classification

problem.claim: Graph classification models use attention- and pooling-based GNNs to extract critical graph features for prediction.

gap.claim: Learning-to-attend methods can absorb statistical correlations without distinguishing causal from noncausal feature effects, causing reliance on noncausal shortcuts that may fail outside the training distribution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Attention- and pooling-based GNNs are prevalent for extracting predictive graph features.
These models generally learn attention by maximizing mutual information between the attended graph and the ground-truth label.
The approach does not distinguish causal from noncausal effects and may absorb all training-data correlations.
The attended graphs may rely on noncausal features as predictive shortcuts.
Shortcuts can change outside the training distribution, resulting in poor generalization.
